original_question: Let f be a homeomorphism in W^{1,p}(Omega, R^n) such that Jf = 1 almost everywhere, so the deformation is incompressible. Can f be approximated in the Sobolev norm by incompressible diffeomorphisms, or by piecewise affine incompressible homeomorphisms?
target_in_paper: The draft is best understood as aiming at the incompressible/volume-preserving variant of the Ball-Evans approximation problem: whether a Sobolev homeomorphism with Jacobian determinant equal to 1 almost everywhere can be strongly approximated in W^{1,p} by volume-preserving diffeomorphisms, and possibly by volume-preserving piecewise affine homeomorphisms, in the same general approximation framework highlighted in the paper's introduction. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2502.01336))
correct_elements: Your draft already gets the core mathematical content right: it asks about a homeomorphism f in W^{1,p}(Omega,R^n), imposes the incompressibility condition Jf=1 a.e., asks for approximation in the Sobolev norm, and singles out exactly the two approximation classes that are central throughout the Ball-Evans literature: diffeomorphisms and piecewise affine homeomorphisms. That is very close to the paper's overall framing of the approximation problem. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2502.01336))
missing_details: The domain/image relation should be made explicit: f should be a homeomorphism f: Omega -> f(Omega) (or Omega -> Delta if the target domain is named separately), not just a map into R^n.
The convergence should be stated as strong convergence in W^{1,p}(Omega,R^n), i.e. ||f_j-f||_{W^{1,p}(Omega,R^n)} -> 0.
The admissible range of p and n should be stated explicitly if the paper restricts them in the relevant formulation; your draft leaves both open.
The exact meaning of 'incompressible diffeomorphism' should be stated: det Df_j = 1 almost everywhere (equivalently everywhere for smooth maps).

If the piecewise affine formulation is included, its meaning should be explicit: each approximant is a homeomorphism that is affine on each simplex/cell of a locally finite triangulation and has determinant 1 on each affine piece.
It should be clarified whether the approximants are required to map Omega onto the same image f(Omega) (or Delta).
If the paper includes uniform convergence and/or boundary agreement together with Sobolev convergence, that should be stated; your draft only mentions the Sobolev norm.
If the paper treats the piecewise affine formulation only as an equivalent reformulation after a separate proposition/theorem, that equivalence should not be assumed unless stated.
If orientation-preservation is stated separately in the paper, it should be included explicitly, even though det Df=1 a.e. already suggests it.
refined_question: Let Omega subset R^n be a domain, let 1 <= p < infinity, and let f: Omega -> f(Omega) be a homeomorphism in W^{1,p}(Omega,R^n) such that det Df = 1 almost everywhere in Omega. Must there exist a sequence of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms f_j: Omega -> f(Omega), with det Df_j = 1, such that f_j -> f strongly in W^{1,p}(Omega,R^n)? If the paper formulates the piecewise affine version in parallel, can one equivalently ask for strong W^{1,p}-approximation by volume-preserving piecewise affine homeomorphisms?
justification: The paper's abstract says that its main topic is the approximation of Sobolev homeomorphisms by diffeomorphisms or piecewise affine homeomorphisms, so the natural paper-faithful refinement is to keep your question narrowly inside that framework while adding the Jacobian-one constraint that encodes incompressibility. ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2502.01336)) The author's publication page confirms that this article is a survey/review paper rather than a new broad generalization, so the refinement should stay close to the standard Ball-Evans approximation format rather than broaden to other nonlinear-elasticity questions. ([www2.karlin.mff.cuni.cz](https://www2.karlin.mff.cuni.cz/~hencl/articles.php?lng=eng)) Because the full internal text of the arXiv paper was not accessible in the retrieved sources, I have kept the reformulation conservative: it sharpens the statement into a stand-alone research question without asserting any unverified extra hypotheses or any unverified equivalence between the diffeomorphic and piecewise affine formulations.
